title: Redelivery and Idempotency Lab
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Learning Record Store
Stream Processing
Idempotency
At-Least-Once Delivery
Deduplication
description: A p5.js lab in which learners deliver statements through an at-least-once stream, crash the processor before it commits, and compare a summary writer that increments with one that recomputes an absolute count from a deduplicated log.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Idempotent ingest: redelivery, deduplication by statement id and absolute summary writes
learningObjectives: The learner will justify why writing absolute values, not increments, keeps a summary correct when statements are redelivered.
prerequisites: Rows and unique keys in a database

accessibility.notes: Native buttons, slider and checkbox; counter values and their offset from the truth are printed as numbers and words, not only as bar lengths or colors

controls.label: Deliver next statement
controls.purpose: Process one delivery (and attempt a commit at a batch boundary)

controls.label: Redelivery chance
controls.purpose: Chance that a batch commit fails and the batch is redelivered

controls.label: Crash before commit
controls.purpose: Force the current batch to be redelivered

controls.label: Deduplicate log by statement id
controls.purpose: Keep one log row per statement id

controls.label: Reset
controls.purpose: Empty the log and both counters

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Contrast two write strategies under the same failures, then justify one
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Step-through delivery with forced and random failures and a layer toggle
keyQuestions: Why can an increment never tell a repeat from a new statement?
Why does an absolute value computed from the log survive any number of rewrites?
When Writer B drifts, which layer failed?
commonMisconceptions: Exactly-once delivery can be assumed from a durable queue
Deduplicating the log alone makes every downstream summary correct
An increment error can be found and fixed later from the summary
assessmentOpportunities: Tracing how Writer A reached its value
Naming the failed layer when deduplication is off

simulation.modelType: Discrete event simulation of at-least-once delivery
equations: Writer A: count = count + 1 per delivery
Writer B: count = rows in the log view (one per statement id when deduplicated)
truth = number of distinct statement ids delivered
assumptions: The offset commit happens when the processor fetches the next batch
A seeded random draw decides whether a commit fails
limitations: ReplacingMergeTree deduplicates eventually at merge time; the lab shows the deduplicated view immediately
Only one summary count is modeled
